title: Color gradients
slide_intent: Teach designers to vary the intensity of a transition without changing the hue’s identity. Comparing endpoints makes the difference between subtle and pronounced gradients visible.
strategic_value: A shared gradient method can create movement within layouts while preserving recognizable palette families.
demonstration: Each hue has two bands: light to mid-tone and light to dark. A separate near-white blend runs to biscuit.
practical_value: Pick a tonal span to suit the desired emphasis and specify process-color endpoints for a standard printed gradient.

content_islands.name: Gradient guidance
content_islands.spec: Place a short principle above the samples and production notes at left.

content_islands.name: Paired tonal ramps
content_islands.spec: Stack two labeled horizontal gradients for each hue and arrange the families in two columns. Keep the light endpoint on the same side throughout.

content_islands.name: Neutral ramps
content_islands.spec: Set the near-white and gray examples alongside the hue families for comparison.
